title: APODICTIC: /adjudicate and /reconstruct
alt: Flowchart. Your manuscript and its Argument State are broken into a claim graph of atomic claims, warrants, qualifiers and typed links, each anchored to your text. In /adjudicate you decide every claim and link: approve it or reject it, and a claim can also be revised in your own words, which makes a new claim that comes back for a decision. Rejections stay excluded, even after later revisions; for now, while any rejection stands, new approvals pause until the semantic exclusion screen is built. Only approved claims and links go into the drafting packet. In /reconstruct a fresh drafter with no tools sees only that packet and returns a new draft with its own passage map, a self-report linking passages to approved claims. The draft comes back for your review and is never marked cleared.

steps.caption: Start from your manuscript and the Argument State the engine built from it.
The argument is broken into a claim graph: each claim, warrant, qualifier and link is one record, anchored to your text.
In /adjudicate you decide every record yourself. Nothing is approved for you, and there is no approve-the-rest.
Approve a claim or link. A claim can also be revised in your own words; the revision is a new claim, so it comes back for a fresh decision.
Reject it, and it stays out: later revisions and re-runs cannot quietly bring it back. For now, while any rejection stands, new approvals pause until the exclusion screen is built.
Only approved claims and links go into the drafting packet.
In /reconstruct a fresh drafter, with no tools and no view of your manuscript, writes from the packet alone.
You get a new draft and the drafter's passage map, its own report of which approved claims each passage uses. It comes back for your review, never marked cleared.
